question: How do I properly attach and tighten the cooling water line fittings for a CP800 Series Compressor?
reference_answer: First, ensure the cooling water supply is turned off. Apply Teflon tape or pipe sealant to the threads of the 1/4" Male National Pipe Thread (MPT) fittings. Attach the fittings to the compressor's water inlet and outlet connections, initially tightening them by hand. Then, use one wrench to keep the compressor's connections from turning while using a second wrench to tighten the fittings until they are snug.

question: What are the steps involved in the automated cool-down process for the attoDRY2100?
reference_answer: The automated cool-down process involves four main steps: 1) The pulse tube precools the system while all valves are closed and the pump is off. 2) When the second cold stage is below 4 K, the scroll pump starts and the 'Cryo In' valve opens. The 'Dump Out' valve also opens if the stage temperature stays below 4.5 K and the condensing line pressure is below 1200 mbar. 3) As pressure drops to 900 mbar or less, the system doses helium into the condensing line by opening and closing the 'Dump Out' valve until the dump pressure reaches 850 mbar. 4) The 'Cryo Out' valve opens to start helium circulation, while the dosing process continues in parallel until the dump pressure drops below 100 mbar.

IV. General procedures 
 Inside the attoDRY2100 a sample is cooled or warmed by a heat conducted 
through a static exchange gas  in the sample space. Temperature of the 
outer wall of sample space is regulated by a constant helium gas flow in VTI

helium is cooled down by the cold head of the PT. The gas passes through a 
cold trap located at the 40K stage, it further liquefies and drops in the liquid 
helium reservoir located below 4K stage. Liquid helium further is pumped 
through a flwo impedance thus it evaporates and cools below 4K. Finally 
helium passes through VTI cooling the sample space and flowing back to the 
pump.  
 
The general prin ciple of the cryostat’s operation is following. The scroll 
pump starts to evacuate the dump through the Dump Out valve (see Figure 
3), pumping helium in the condensing line with open ‘Cryo In’ valve when: 
(a) the PT’s cold head is at its base temperature, (b) sample space evacuated 
and filled with exchange gas, (c) the VTI and condensing lines are pumped 
out (no air inside). ‘Dump Out ’ valve opens and c loses according to a 
constantly monitored pressure in the condensing line.

 The automated cooling down process has the following steps: 
1) Pulse tube precools the system, all valves are closed and the pump 
is turned off. 
2) When the temperature of the second cold stage (or the 
temperature of the magnet) is below 4  K, scroll pump starts and 
‘Cryo In’ valve opens up. Dump Out valve opens if the temperature 
of the second cold stage stays below 4.5  K and when the pressure 
in the condensing line is below 1200 mbar.  
3) Slowly dropping pressure in the condensing line indicates helium 
condensation. When it drops to 900  mbar or below and when 
second cold stage temperature is below 4.5 K, helium will be dosed 
in the condensing line by opening and closing Dump Ou t. This 
process of helium dosing in the condensing line continues until the 
dump pressure decreases to 850 mbar.

cryostat through the scroll pump. Dosing of the helium in the 
condensing line c ontinues in parallel to the circulation until the 
dump pressure drops below 100 mbar.

question: How do I perform Test #1 to check if the helium circulation line was properly evacuated?
reference_answer: First, start a new log with a 5s sampling time. Then, open all four electronic valves and use an external turbo pump to evacuate the helium circulation line down to approximately e-4 mbar. After that, close the black mechanical valve, close all electronic valves except for the cryo-out valve, and turn off the scroll pump. Finally, monitor the pressures in the GUI for 30 minutes; they should all be less than 5e-2 mbar.

question: What is the complete procedure for evacuating the helium circulation lines and heating the Zeolith trap during a preventive maintenance cleaning?
reference_answer: First, ensure the cryostat is shut down, warm (magnet > 290 K), and the compressor is off. Then, connect an external turbo pump to the dump's pumping port. Start the external pump and open the manual valve. Next, open all four electromagnetic valves and start the scroll pump. Plug in the Zeolith trap heater for exactly 20 minutes. Finally, let the external pump run for at least 12 hours until the pressure drops below 5-7 x 10⁻⁵ mbar.

VI. Preventive Maintenance 
VI.1. Cleaning Cold Trap and Condensing Line. 
 Helium circulation lines of attoDRY2100 have several trapping station to 
prevent dirt from entering a condenser located at 4  K-stage. They are a 
Zeolith trap located at the outlet of Scroll pump and the cold trap located 
at the first (40 K) stage of PT (see Figure 3). If there are no external leaks in 
the system, a clog could build up over long time or in case of cold trap warm 
up (possibly due to compressor power or cooling water failure, or due to 
magnet quench) leading to a gradual increase of ‘Cryo in’ pressure and to a 
cooling power loss. At this state the sample temperature will rise and it 
won’t be controllable anymore. To prevent clogging and thus 
malfunctioning of the cryostat we recommend cleani ng up the condensing 
line between operational cycles, when the entire system is warm and turned 
off. Depending on the intensity of usage of the cryostat a cleaning should 
be performed ones in 3 -6 months. Following steps will guide you through 
cleaning procedure: 
1. Shut down the cryostat. When all helium is back to the dump, turn off the compressor and cooling 
water. 
2. Ensure the magnet (4 K-Stage of PT) temperature is above 290 K. Depending on the configuration of 
the cryostat entire warming process might take from one to four days. 
3. Using KF25 clamp connect an external turbo and roughing pump to the pumping port located at top 
of the dump. 
4. Start external turbo pump and open manual KF25 valve at top of the dump.  
5. Open all four electromagnetic valves and start the scroll pump ether from expert mode of the touch 
screen or from GUI. 
6. Plug the heater of Zeolith trap in power socket for 20 minutes. Further actions can be performed 
without waiting.  Important: To avoid overheating of Zeolith keep the heater on for 20 min utes only. 
7. Keep external pump running for at least 12 hours. Due to narrow and long piping of condensing line 
we recommend pumping it at least 12 hours. After that time ensure that a pressure gauge at 
external turbo pump shows values below 5-7 x 10-5 mbar. 
8. Close all four electromagnetic valves and stop the scroll pump ether from expert mode of the touch 
screen or from GUI. 
9. Close the manual pumping port on top of the dump. Connect a bottle with pure pressurized helium 
gas (purity level 5.0 - 99.999%) to the pumping port on top of the dump and evacuate all dead 
volumes between helium nozzle, external turbo pump and manual pumping port.  
10. After filling line is pumped to 10-5 mbar range, close the turbo pump, open helium bottle and open 
pumping port on top of the dump to fill 900-1000 mbar of helium into the dump.

question: A user reports a 'Defective Hardware' error and a red blinking pressure status LED. What is the specific hardware component that has likely failed, and what are the software-based or reboot procedures that can be attempted to clear this error before replacing the part?
reference_answer: The 'Defective Hardware' error, when accompanied by a red blinking pressure status LED, indicates a failure of the cryo-in pressure gauge (Passage A). Before replacing the physical component, one could first attempt to clear the error message from the system. This can be done by either clicking 'lower error' in the software, or by disconnecting the USB cable between the magnet power supply (MPS) and the controller box and then rebooting the controller box (Passage B).

question: What is the procedure for setting the current in a shim coil for the first time, starting from a fully dumped state?
reference_answer: First, select the shim to be set using the [Down] or [Shift-Up] softkey. Press the [Pers Htr] and [Confirm Htr On] softkeys to turn on the persistent switch heater and wait about 10 seconds for it to warm up. Next, press the [Limit] softkey to energize the shim coil to the desired current. After the limit is reached, turn the persistent switch heater off by pressing [Pers Htr] and [Confirm Htr Off], and wait another 10 seconds for it to cool. Finally, press the [Zero] key to return the current in the power leads to zero.

question: What are the steps to evacuate the isolation vacuum on an attoDRY cryostat, starting from when the system is fully warmed up?
reference_answer: First, ensure the cryostat is fully warmed up (above 280 K). Open the front cover and connect the turbo pump to the isolation vacuum port. Switch on the pump, then open the manual valve to begin pumping. Allow the pump to run for at least 4 hours or until the pressure is below 5x10e-3 mbar. Once the target vacuum is reached, close the manual valve, switch off the turbo pump, disconnect it, and finally, close the front cover.

question: How do I safely connect the magnet power leads to the APS100 power supply?
reference_answer: First, ensure the APS100 power is OFF. Then, attach the power leads to the I(+) and I(-) terminals on the rear panel, securing them with a ¼-20 bolt and nut to ensure a solid contact. Crucially, never disconnect the magnet leads when current is present, as this can create a potentially lethal voltage.

question: What is the procedure for manually warming up the entire attoDRY system to room temperature?
reference_answer: To warm up the system, first manually switch off the compressor but keep the cooling water cycling. Do not use the 'shut down' function. Next, manually open the dump-in valve and close the cryo-in valve, while keeping the scroll pump running. The cryo-out valve should stay open and the dump-out valve must be closed. After 3-4 hours, you can stop the scroll pump and then wait for the system to reach room temperature.

question: What is the procedure for removing excess helium from the compressor package if the system pressure is too high?
reference_answer: First, confirm that the lowest reading pressure gauge on the compressor exceeds the pressure specified in Appendix A. If it does, proceed with the following steps: 1) Ensure the service valve on the front panel is fully closed by turning it clockwise. 2) Attach the ¼" service Aeroquip coupling to the service access. 3) Slowly open the service valve by turning it counter-clockwise, venting no more than 5 PSIG of gas per minute. 4) Observe the gauge with the lower reading until it reaches the specified system helium pressure. 5) Close the service valve by turning it clockwise and then remove the service Aeroquip from the service access.

question: What is the step-by-step process for inserting a new sample and preparing it for cooldown?
reference_answer: First, maintain a helium overpressure in the sample space. After inserting the new sample, close the sample space with a KF50 clamp. Then, evacuate and flush the space with helium. Next, add 700-1000 mbar of exchange gas into the sample space at room temperature. Finally, press the confirmation message on the touch screen to turn off the VTI heater and begin the cooldown process.

question: How do I perform a full evacuation of the GHS system, including flushing the helium line?
reference_answer: First, ensure the GHS is connected, the product is warm, and the 'Expert' screen is open. Then, open all valves via the touch panel and start the scroll pump. On the external turbo pump, close the needle valve, open the dump's manual valve, open the main valve, and switch it on. Let the system pump for at least 10-12 hours until the vacuum pressure is below 3x10e-4 mbar. After reaching the target pressure, close the dump's manual valve and the turbo pump's main valve. To flush the helium line, open the helium bottle valve, the turbo pump's needle valve, and all manual valves on the helium line. Then, close the helium bottle valve and open the turbo pump's main valve to remove the helium. This flushing process must be repeated.

The APS100 shim supply option is designed for ease of use and to allow the user to set shim coils using a minimum of 
keystrokes.  It provides considerable flexibility in setup and operation.  There are built-in interlocks that reduce the risk 
of accidental dumping of a shim or quenching of a coil.  However, it is still necessary for the operator to be familiar and 
experienced with shimming to reduce the chance of errors.  It is highly recommended that the operator familiarize

H.3.1  MANUAL Mode  
Mutual inductance coupling between shim coils and the main superconducting coil is inevitable.  Due to this coupling, 
if the main coil is energized or discharged while the shim coils are in persistent mode, significant current can be 
induced in the shim coils.  If this current is not periodically “dumped” during the main coil charge cycle, it can build to 
the point where a quench of the shim coil and/or the main coil occurs. 
 
The APS100 shim supply option is designed to periodically scan through the shims installed in the system to dump the 
current induced in them during main coil charge or discharge.  Dumping a shim coil involves activating the persistent 
switch heater on the shim coil for a period of several seconds.  By effectively quenching the persistent switch, the loop 
is “opened” and any current induced in the coil is converted to heat and is dissipated.  While dumping shim coils it is 
usually a good idea to connect a low resistance (~ 5 ohms) load across the main current leads on the shim coils to 
prevent large voltage spikes from occurring. 
 
The APS100 shim option will step through each of the 12 shim coil heater outputs in the system.  The unit activates 
each heater for approximately 6 seconds – long enough for the persistent switch to change to its “normal” state.  
Scanning of the shim coil heaters to dump them during main coil energizing or discharge may be inhibited by 
activating the global inhibit command while in manual mode.

question: How can I avoid the risk of electrical shock when connecting or disconnecting cables from the electronics?
reference_answer: To avoid the risk of electrical shock, you must ensure the electronics are turned off before connecting or unplugging any cables. The manual warns to never connect cabling when the electronics are on.
